title: Section 22
commentary:
Section 22 governs the deductions allowable while computing income under the head “Income from house property”. First, a statutory standard deduction of 30% of the annual value determined under section 21 is allowed under sub-section (1)(a). Second, sub-section (1)(b) allows deduction for interest payable on capital borrowed for acquiring, constructing, repairing, renewing, or reconstructing the property. When interest relates to the pre-acquisition or pre-construction period, sub-section (1)(c) permits it to be deducted in five equal instalments beginning from the tax year of acquisition or construction, subject to reduction under sub-section (3) for any amount already deducted under the Act.

For properties referred to in section 21(6), interest deductions face statutory ceilings under sub-sections (2) and (5). A maximum deduction of ₹2,00,000 is allowed if the borrowed capital was for acquisition or construction completed within five years from the end of the borrowing tax year, evidenced by a certificate specifying details under sub-section (4). In any other case (such as repairs or exceeding the time limit), the cap is ₹30,000. Under sub-section (6), interest payable outside India is disallowed unless tax is paid or deducted, or an agent exists in India.

Interpretation: The ₹2,00,000 threshold under sub-section (5) operates as an aggregate ceiling across all properties governed by section 21(6), rather than an individual limit per property.

example.assumptions: All figures are illustrative assumptions: Let-out house property with annual value under section 21 of ₹6,00,000; current year interest payable on borrowed construction capital of ₹1,40,000; total prior-period interest accumulated prior to the tax year of construction completion of ₹1,00,000 (with no prior deductions claimed).
example.scenario: An assessee computes taxable income from a let-out residential house property constructed using borrowed capital, claiming statutory deductions and loan interest for the current tax year.
example.walkthrough: Step 1: Compute the statutory deduction under section 22(1)(a) at 30% of the annual value (30% of ₹6,00,000 = ₹1,80,000). Step 2: Determine current year interest payable under section 22(1)(b), which equals ₹1,40,000. Step 3: Compute the pre-construction interest instalment under section 22(1)(c) and section 22(3) in five equal parts (₹1,00,000 / 5 = ₹20,000). Step 4: Total deductions under section 22 equal ₹3,40,000 (₹1,80,000 + ₹1,40,000 + ₹20,000), resulting in net income under this head of ₹2,60,000.
example.takeaway: Income from house property is computed by reducing 30% of the annual value, current interest on borrowed capital, and one-fifth of allowable pre-construction interest.

mcqs.question: What is the standard deduction rate applicable on the annual value under section 22(1)(a)?
mcqs.explanation: Section 22(1)(a) specifically provides a deduction equal to 30% of the annual value as determined under section 21. The other percentages are not mentioned in the text.

mcqs.question: Interest payable for the period prior to the tax year of acquisition or construction is deductible in how many equal instalments under section 22(1)(c)?
mcqs.explanation: Section 22(1)(c) provides that such prior-period interest is deductible in five equal instalments starting from the tax year of acquisition or construction and the four immediately succeeding tax years.

mcqs.question: What is the maximum interest deduction allowable under section 22(2)(b) for a property referred to in section 21(6) where borrowed capital was utilized for repair or renewal?
mcqs.explanation: Under section 22(2)(b), the deduction shall not exceed ₹30,000 in any other case (which includes repairs or renewals). The ₹2,00,000 limit in section 22(2)(a) applies strictly to acquisition or construction.

mcqs.question: To qualify for the enhanced interest deduction limit of ₹2,00,000 under section 22(2)(a), within what timeframe must the acquisition or construction be completed?
options: Within 3 years from the date of borrowing capital
Within 5 years from the end of the tax year in which capital was borrowed
Within 5 years from the end of the calendar year of borrowing
Within 7 years from the date the construction commences
mcqs.explanation: Section 22(2)(a)(i) requires that acquisition or construction must be completed within five years from the end of the tax year in which capital was borrowed.

mcqs.question: Under section 22(6), interest payable outside India is disallowed as a deduction if which of the following conditions is satisfied?
options: Tax has not been paid or deducted under Chapter XIX-B and there is no agent in India as per section 306
The loan has been sanctioned by a foreign entity without prior approval
The loan is not repaid within five years from the date of borrowing
The interest payable exceeds the aggregate cap of ₹2,00,000
mcqs.explanation: Section 22(6) disallows deduction for interest payable outside India if tax has not been paid or deducted on such interest under Chapter XIX-B and there is no agent in India as per section 306.

mnemonics.tip: Use 'ACRRR' to remember the five permissible purposes for borrowing capital under section 22(1)(b) that qualify for interest deduction.
